newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary to invite bids for K&H bank by Jan 15.
newsitem.headline: Hungary to invite bids for K&H bank by Jan 15.

text.p: Hungary's state privatisation agency APV said on Wednesday it would publish a tender for the sale of an at least 25 percent plus one vote stake in Kereskedelmi Bank Rt (K&H), the country's third largest commercial bank, by January 15.
"A closed, two-round tender must be published for strategic investors (bank, financial institution or internationally recognised insurance company) by January 15, 1997," APV said.

The investors should acquire the stake through buying shares and increasing the bank's capital, APV said, adding that it would select those investors entitled to carry out due diligence at K&H in the first round.
The tender must enable financial investors to cooperate with strategic investors in the bank's privatisation, APV said.
APV added it would also publish a tender by March 1 for financial investors to raise the capital of K&H by $40 million.

The strategic investor that wins the first tender is to carry out the capital increase at the the annual general meeting of K&H shareholders next spring, while financial investors must complete the capital increase by May 31.
Following the strategic investor's capital increase, shares of 519.8 million forint nominal value would be offered to K&H management and employees with preferential conditions, APV said.
Hungary will also transfer a stake in K&H to the social security funds. The Finance Minister will decide on the number of such shares by February 28, APV said.

The remaining shares will be offered to domestic small investors publicly by December 31, 1997, APV said, adding that a yet-to-be-decided part of those shares should be offered for compensation coupons.
Compensation coupons have been issued to victims of fascism and communism since 1992.
